title: Graph Neural Bandits

problem.claim: Contextual bandit algorithms select arms using contextual information while balancing exploitation and exploration.

gap.claim: Existing works estimate rigid user clusters, which does not represent fine-grained collaborative effects.

contributions.claim: A Graph Neural Bandits framework leverages collaboration among users through graph neural networks for online recommendation scenarios.
The framework models fine-grained collaborative effects through estimated user graphs for exploitation and exploration.
Separate GNN-based models are used on estimated user graphs for exploitation and adaptive exploration.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The paper reports theoretical analysis and experiments on multiple real data sets against state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report that these analyses and experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: Contextual bandits select high-reward arms using contextual information and address exploitation-exploration tradeoffs.
The paper proposes Graph Neural Bandits to exploit user collaboration with graph neural networks in online recommendation.
The framework replaces rigid user-cluster estimation with fine-grained collaborative effects represented by estimated user graphs.
Separate GNN-based models refine exploitation and adaptive exploration on the estimated user graphs.
The authors report theoretical and multi-dataset experimental comparisons with state-of-the-art baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method represents user collaboration with estimated graphs rather than rigid clusters.

interpretation.claim: Adaptive relational representations may capture heterogeneous collaborative effects more precisely than coarse grouping.

application.claim: Consider graph-based user representations when recommendation behavior depends on fine-grained relationships.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when estimated graphs outperform clustering or how graph estimation errors affect performance.

source_observation.claim: Exploitation and adaptive exploration use separate GNN-based models.

interpretation.claim: Separating the two objectives may allow their relational signals to be modeled differently.

application.claim: For sequential recommendation, evaluate whether distinct models for exploitation and exploration improve decision strategies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the model architectures, training procedure, or conditions under which separate models are beneficial.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide theoretical guarantees or their assumptions.
The abstract does not identify the real data sets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe graph estimation, GNN architectures, or training and exploration procedures.
